independent_controls: Explicit halfwidth voiced, semi-voiced, small-vowel, mixed-width punctuation, fullwidth spacing/combining marks and voiced WA/WO outputs are original literal goldens, without invoking the implementation to derive expected values.
Reversing the two existing standalone operations on halfwidth voiced input produces Katakana rather than Hiragana; the supported 36 route therefore pins the selected engineering order.
Derived nullable fields, correlated calls, numeric-to-Text UNION promotion and retained CVar/LeftB LenB/AscW consumers exercise actual bound-query paths.
Exact1041, unsupported LCIDs/aliases/combinations, eager operational failures, NULL and malformed Unicode retain existing validation order; the public Conversion recipe still refuses 36.
Every observed scalar cancellation checkpoint, cumulative zero-byte/zero-step failures and actual width output expansion beyond the per-Text limit are checked. Both stages share the caller allowance.

primary_references.use: Describes flag values and nonexclusive combinations; does not define universal conversion ordering or independently establish direct query availability.
Explicitly requires FULLWIDTH with HIRAGANA to map halfwidth Katakana to Hiragana; standalone HIRAGANA preserves halfwidth Katakana.
Documents FULLWIDTH voiced composition, such as fullwidth spacing voiced marks composing with their kana base.

qualification: This is a TableCraft engineering composition informed by specific Microsoft mapping behavior. The published general StrConv combination rule does not establish a universal operation order; no native Access StrConv or Windows NLS equivalence is claimed.
limits: Only exact conversion36 is newly admitted. All other previously unsupported width/kana/case/encoding combinations remain refused.
Existing standalone width/kana mapping restrictions apply unchanged. No general normalization, automatic locale or new mapping table is introduced.
Legacy public Conversion component recipes remain unchanged; the complete operation is private evaluator dispatch.
Intermediate width Text and final Hiragana Text each consume existing limits and cumulative allocations; budgets are not reset or refunded.
